description:
FILED s536g (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-08) while probing #4222 / #4602.  PRE-EXISTING (c8886b61 and ba7863a3 die too; the message changed with s536g's split from `&main::-Foo` to `&main::bar`).

    print -Foo::bar, "\n";
    package Foo; sub bar { 3 } package main; print -Foo::bar, "\n";
      perl 5.40.3:  -Foo::bar / -3
      PCL:          dies "Undefined subroutine &main::bar called" (base: "&main::-Foo")

PPI (vendored 1.292, branch `pcl`) tokens: Word<-Foo> Word<::bar> -- the negative-bareword Word stops at the first `::`.  perl's toke.c reads `-` then the identifier `Foo::bar`; PPI's own `-bareword` reading should take the whole qualified name (`-Foo::bar` as ONE Word, which PExpr::_split_negated_call_words then splits like `-NAME`).  A PPI bug for the vendored branch (principle 13: a row in docs/ppi-bug-report.t + t/ppi_bugs_pcl.t, the fix on `pcl`), not a Pl/ repair.  Once one Word arrives, `_split_negated_call_words` must accept a qualified NAME (its regex is `\A-([A-Za-z_]\w*)\z` today) and ask `_bareword_callable_here` with the qualified name (it handles `Pkg::name`).

=== s536g addendum (the wide A/B) ===
The same mis-lex hits the `CORE::` spelling, and there it is a REAL module's failure: core Math::Complex lines 750 (`-CORE::exp(CORE::log(-$z)/3)`) and 1081 (`my $v = -CORE::log($alpha + CORE::sqrt(...))`).

    my $z = 1; my $v = -CORE::log($z + CORE::sqrt(4)); print "$v ", -CORE::exp(0), "\n";
      perl 5.40.3:  -1.09861228866811 -1
      PCL (ba7863a3 and s536g):  dies "Undefined subroutine &main::log called"

PPI tokens: Word<-CORE> Word<::log> List<(...)>.  With the PPI fix (`-CORE::log` as ONE Word), `_split_negated_call_words` must accept a qualified NAME and treat `CORE::NAME` as callable (the `_core_qualified` marker path).  Priority up: this is a die in a core module's function bodies (Math::Complex's cbrt / acosh family).

=== DONE (s536j) ===
FIXED on PCL's PPI branch: group AV, commit ce2aaa80 (tests e0f12cd1) on branch pcl -- PPI::Token::DashedWord reads the package-qualified tail with PPI::Token::Word's name pattern after the filetest test, so `-Foo::bar`, `-CORE::log`, `-foo::bar::baz`, `-Foo::`, `-a::b` are one Word; `-e::foo` stays the filetest on ::foo (toke.c yyl_hyphen).  Catalogue docs/ppi-upstream-bugs.md §62, registry row 62 (fixed_in pcl), report rows 373-382.
PCL half: Pl::PExpr::_split_negated_call_words (s536g's) accepts a qualified NAME (`\A-([A-Za-z_]\w*(?:::\w+)*)(::)?\z`) and splits `-Foo::` into `-` + the package word (perl: "-Foo"); NEW Pl::PExpr::_qualified_word_callable, asked by the fat-comma quoting (cleanup_for_parsing) and both subscript autoquotes (the cleanup hash-brace pass and _subscript_autoquote_text): perl quotes an IDENTIFIER only, so `(Foo::bar => 1)`, `$h{Foo::bar}`, `$h{-Foo::bar}` CALL a declared Foo::bar (keys 3 / -3, probed) and an undeclared one stays the string.
Probes perl -> main -> tree (scratch/s536j/p/n1.pl n2.pl n4.pl n5.pl mc.pl mc2.pl): tree = perl on all; main died on every one.  Core Math::Complex: cbrt(-8), acos(2), cplx(1,1)**2 = perl.  Guard Pl/t/ppi-token-rows-01.t r25-r28 (FAIL on 3139fcb0).  Wide A/B vs 3139fcb0: the ONE moved file is Math/Complex.pm (its -CORE:: sites 737 750 1058 1081 left the detector table and are calls).
Found beside it, PRE-EXISTING, filed #4762: `my $y = Foo::nob;` (no strict, undeclared) is CALLED where perl reads the string.


=== COMPLETED (s538, the reviewing session) === merged with s536j = MAIN-READY-86 d2e4ba52 (PPI pcl c2f21706), 2026-11-11.
subject: PPI lexes a NEGATED QUALIFIED bareword `-Foo::bar` / `-CORE::log(...)` as two Words `-Foo` + `::bar`, so PCL dies "Undefined subroutine" (core Math::Complex lines 750 + 1081 die; perl: -(CORE::log(...)), or the string "-Foo::bar")
